findings.summary: Two tests use process.cwd() as the 'outside tmpdir' path: removeFixtureDir(process.cwd()) and a symlink to process.cwd(). When the repo is checked out under tmpdir() (sandboxed agent, CI runner or remote session cloning into /tmp, or a custom TMPDIR), the guard sees the target as inside tmpdir and recursively deletes the working checkout before the expect(...).toThrow fails. This is the data loss the task exists to prevent. Fix: build the outside path from dirname(realpathSync(tmpdir())) as a path that doesn't exist, or skip these tests when realpathSync(process.cwd()) is inside realpathSync(tmpdir()).

findings.summary: OUTSIDE = dirname(realpathSync(tmpdir())) is an existing directory ('/' on Linux, /private/var/folders/<xx> on macOS). The refuses-outside, refuses-parent and symlink-to-outside tests pass this real path to removeFixtureDir. Today the guard refuses it correctly, but if a future edit breaks the guard these tests would run rmSync(recursive) on '/' or the user's temp parent before the toThrow assertion fails. Suggestion: point the refuse-path and symlink tests at a nonexistent path under OUTSIDE, e.g. join(OUTSIDE, 'rfd-never-exists-<rand>'). No exploit while the guard is correct, so this does not block.

findings.summary: realOrResolved() slices with abs.slice(parent.length + 1). When the parent is the filesystem root, this drops one extra character ('/foo' becomes '/oo'). The result still lands outside tmpdir so the guard refuses (fail-closed) and nothing is deleted. Correctness nit only; use path.relative(parent, abs) or basename(abs).
